STEP 1 - Scene: A meal of cooked bacon strips (crispy pan-fried bacon) on a plate, nothing else visible.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white square plate, roughly 22 cm across (side length). Area ≈ 22 x 22 ≈ 484 cm^2, treated as a ~24 cm dinner-plate-equivalent, so I use ~480 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Cooked bacon strips (one item).

STEP 4 - Area: Bacon covers roughly 35% of the plate area, a loose pile with gaps between strips.

STEP 5 - Volume: 0.35 x 480 ≈ 168 cm^2 footprint. Pile height averages about 1 cm (strips are stacked in a few layers). Gross volume ≈ 168 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Bacon is a meat item with a bulk density around 0.9 g/ml when cooked and crisp, but the bulk density here is lower because the strips are thin and irregular. Using 0.9 g/ml: 168 x 0.9 ≈ 150 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked pan-fried bacon ≈ 540 kcal per 100 g. 150 g x 5.4 ≈ 810 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Roughly 150 g of cooked bacon (about 8 to 10 strips) is plausible for the visible pile on a plate of this size. Cooked bacon is very fatty and calorie-dense, so ~800 kcal fits. Estimate is approximate; the uncertainty is mainly in pile height.
